what: It makes the Oura Ring, a smart ring, and a membership app that turns body data into health insights.
proceeds: Oura expects about $532.6 million in net proceeds. It plans to use about $526.4 million to pay taxes owed when employee stock units vest at the IPO. The rest is for general business costs such as technology, working capital and equipment.
risks: Its fast growth may not last, and revenue could grow more slowly or fall in the future.
If it cannot win new members and keep current ones, its business and growth will suffer.
It competes with larger companies that have more money, bigger brands and stronger sales networks.
It has only recently become profitable and may not stay profitable as costs rise.
If it cannot keep launching new and improved products and features, its business could be hurt.
